items.summary: Calibration release: the package's no-shipped-coefficients policy finally comes with the tool that closes the loop. Every shipped set carries the caveat that lever arms depend on material, mode pair, excitation and substrate; calibrate_lever_arms turns reference measurements you control -- a strain-stage sweep, a gated sweep, any points with known (strain, density) -- into your own fitted coefficient matrix, with uncertainties and provenance. New in ramansep.calibration calibrate_lever_arms : weighted least-squares fit of the (m, 2) lever-arm matrix, one linear problem per mode on the shared reference design. With shift sigmas the parameter covariance is the exact known-noise Gauss-Markov result and a per-mode chi-square consistency check comes back with it; without sigmas the covariance uses the residual variance, which is why that path refuses fewer than three reference points instead of inventing an error bar. Identifiability refused, not fudged : reference states collinear in the (strain, density) plane (a strain-only sweep, or gating that strains proportionally) cannot separately determine the two arms of any mode -- the fit raises with an explanation instead of returning one of infinitely many minimizers. CalibrationResult.coefficients() packages a two-mode calibration as a ModeCoefficients with a MANDATORY provenance string; result.K feeds MultiModeModel directly for m > 2. Anchors (asserted in the tests, not stated) Noise-free shifts from a known matrix are recovered to machine precision, with zero estimated uncertainty. The hand-built normal-equation solution agrees with an independent QR solve ( numpy.linalg.lstsq on the whitened system) to 1e-10. The orthogonal unit design {(1,0), (0,1)} with unit sigmas has EXACTLY the identity parameter covariance -- the closed form, not an approximation. Seeded Monte-Carlo scatter of the fitted arms matches the reported sigmas. Degenerate and malformed reference sets raise (collinear designs, n = 1, n = 2 without sigmas, non-positive sigmas, non-finite shifts). The full round trip -- calibrate on synthetic references, package the coefficients, invert forward-generated maps through SeparationModel -- returns the input strain and density maps to 1e-10. 50 tests across Python 3.9-3.13. Install: pip install -U ramansep .

To view all available pipelines, just search "warp" in the Dockstore search and browse the workflow list. See Dockstore documentation for details on launching the workflow. items.summary: SlideRule is an open source server-side framework for on-demand processing of science data in the cloud. The SlideRule project offers a new paradigm for NASA archival data management – rapid delivery of customizable on-demand data products, rather than hosting large volumes of standard derivative products, which will inevitably be insufficient for some science applications. The scalable server-side components of SlideRule run in the AWS cloud with optimized functions to read HDF5 data hosted by NASA in S3 cloud object storage. While SlideRule can be accessed by any HTTP client (e.g., curl) through GET and POST requests, the sliderule-python client provides a user-friendly API for synchronous interaction with the SlideRule service. The client library returns standard Python data containers (i.e., Pandas DataFrame) and facilitates serialization with provenance metadata for reproducible science. SlideRule uses a plugin framework to support different NASA missions and data products. The ICESat-2 SlideRule plugin offers customizable algorithms to process the archive of low-level data products from the NASA Ice Cloud and land Elevation Satellite-2 (ICESat-2) laser altimetry mission. The user defines a geographic area of interest and key processing parameters via an interactive web interface or the API, and SlideRule returns high-level surface elevation point cloud products in seconds to minutes, enabling rapid algorithm development, visualization and scientific interpretation.

items.summary: L'Ange des projections lumineuses was a monthly journal published for the Œuvre des projections catéchistiques of Champtercier (Basses-Alpes), printed at Lyon, and edited by the abbé Georges Aillaud. It ran from 15 October 1902 to 15 September 1903 as the organ of a subscription lending library that circulated magic-lantern slide sets to village clergy, together with the technical advice, lecture texts and equipment notices needed to use them. This deposit is a complete transcription of the ten issues held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France — 198 pages. Numbers 10 and 11, July and August 1903, are absent from the BnF holdings and no copies have been located elsewhere. The journal documents a working provincial distribution network at the moment cinema was arriving in rural France: it lists the slide sets in circulation and their prices, reports what was shown and where, argues over illuminants and apparatus, and by its final number is advertising a cinematograph alongside the lantern equipment. Its technical columns are a detailed record of alcohol, Auer and acetylene illumination in non-commercial exhibition. Method. The text was read from the BnF's page images by a vision language model working on overlapping half-page tiles, without optical character recognition, and then compared word by word by machine against the BnF's own OCR text layer wherever one exists. 1,864 disagreements were found across the 150 pages with a text layer, classified automatically, and checked selectively — not exhaustively — against the page images; eight readings were corrected as a result, and a separate audit for digital artefacts produced a further fifty. Every correction is logged with its evidence. This is machine transcription with editorial checking: it has not been proofread cover to cover against the original and should not be described as though it had. The February, March and April 1903 issues have no BnF text layer, rest on a single reading, and are identified as such. Spelling, accentuation, capitalisation and punctuation follow the page, including where the printing is inconsistent with itself. Contents of this deposit. The reading edition as PDF (119 pp.) and as plain UTF-8 text, both carrying the editorial note as front matter; the per-page source files, which preserve the printed line breaks and their end-of-line hyphens, with the flags raised on each page and a separate folder for the eighteen non-journal leaves; the editorial note; an apparatus of 137 unresolved or adjudicated readings; the full correction log; and the complete uncurated production log, labelled as provenance documentation rather than an apparatus. See README.md. Source. Bibliothèque nationale de France, shelfmark D-72088 (BIS); ISSN 2273-6220; BnF catalogue record cb326930724. Page images: Source gallica.bnf.fr / Bibliothèque nationale de France . Rights. The journal text is in the public domain. The editorial note, annotations, arrangement and other original editorial contributions are licensed under CC BY 4.0 . No copyright is asserted over the underlying public-domain text. Related. A prose introduction to the journal — its publisher, the slide network it served, and its bearing on the arrival of cinema in provincial France — was published at the time of this deposit at billlefurgy.com/ange-des-projections-lumineuses . It is not part of this deposit and is not covered by the method statement above.
items.title: L'Ange des projections lumineuses: Transcription of the Ten Issues Held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France, 1902–1903

items.summary: As large language models (LLMs) become widely deployed, their outputs can be copied, transformed, and redistributed at scale without reliable evidence of origin, creating risks for trust, accountability, intellectual property (IP) protection, and high-stakes decision-making. LLM watermarking addresses this problem by embedding detectable signals into text during or after generation. However, existing methods vary in design assumptions, threat models, and evaluation criteria, while deployment choices such as watermark placement, detection authority, and key management affect reliability, security, and scalability. This paper systematizes LLM watermarking as provenance infrastructure for large-scale data ecosystems. We organize existing approaches along four deployment dimensions: insertion point, verification authority, operational state, and transformation threat model, and relate them to the big data requirements of Volume, Velocity, Variety, Veracity, and Value. We further introduce a Big Data Watermarking Readiness framework centered on four deployment workloads: online generation, streaming detection, transformation pipelines, and ecosystem governance. The framework connects these workloads to system-level requirements including throughput, false-positive control, robustness, cross-domain reliability, governance, and downstream utility. Our analysis highlights a gap between benchmark performance and deployment readiness: false positives accumulate at scale, repeated transformations weaken watermark signals, computational overhead can limit online deployment, and centralized verification can create governance bottlenecks. We conclude with an evaluation blueprint and research directions for scalable, trustworthy provenance in big data ecosystems.
items.title: LLM Watermarking as Big Data Provenance: A Deployment-Oriented Systematization

items.summary: Benchmark contamination, where evaluation examples appear in a model's training data, threatens the validity of LLM assessment. Statistical tools for detecting training-data membership exist, but have been validated almost exclusively in controlled academic regimes: large, homogeneous pre-training corpora and transparent, single-stage training pipelines. Whether these methods remain reliable in realistic auditing scenarios remains unclear. We identify two under-studied failure modes: distribution shift, which arises when suspect and validation sets violate the IID assumption, and scale constraints, which arise because benchmarks are orders of magnitude smaller than pre-training corpora. We systematically evaluate three leading paradigms, LLM Dataset Inference, Post-Hoc Dataset Inference, and CoDeC, across 25 models from multiple families (including Pythia, OLMo 2, and specialised cultural and medical LLMs) and scales (up to 27B). We then further extend our analysis to frontier industry models. Across 335 evaluations, only 201 yield correct outcomes. LLM Dataset Inference results in false positives under distribution shift, Post-Hoc Dataset Inference is underpowered at benchmark scale, and CoDeC provides only coarse provenance signals that are insufficient to verify individual benchmark splits. Our results reveal a systematic reliability gap between controlled validation and practical benchmark auditing, and show that statistical detection cannot yet replace transparent data provenance. We open-source our benchmark for further research.
items.title: The Reliability Gap in Benchmark Auditing: Distribution Shift and Scale as Failure Modes of Contamination Detection

items.summary: AI deployment increasingly resembles a pipeline of data transformation, fine-tuning, and agent interactions rather than a monolithic LLM job; recent examples include RLHF/RLAIF training and agentic workflows. To cope with this shift, we propose FlowMesh, a multi-tenant service fabric that executes and optimizes these workloads as one shared service instead of isolated pipelines. It decomposes workflows into fine-grained operators with recorded lineage, enabling de-duplication of work across users and batching requests on the same hardware while preserving per-workflow provenance. A global control plane maintains a cluster-wide pool of ready operators and uses a single utility function to pick both the batch and the worker, balancing throughput, cost, and data locality on heterogeneous GPUs. The data plane is an elastic fleet of stateless workers backed by a content-addressable store, enabling rapid, automatic scale-out, safe retry after preemption, and portability across managed clusters such as Kubernetes and geo-distributed GPU marketplaces such as Vast.ai. Compared with baseline solutions, FlowMesh achieves up to 3.8x cost reduction and 2.0x lower energy usage, provides a similar or better latency profile, and remains efficient under dynamic and failure-prone conditions.
items.title: FlowMesh: A Service Fabric for Composable LLM Workflows

items.summary: Python package and command-line tool that estimates the share of variance in an antimicrobial resistance phenotype carried by the lineages of a bacterial collection, from a lineage label and a susceptibility call or a recorded dilution, and refuses the estimate where the collection cannot support one. One collection admits three quantities and the package reports them apart: the lineage-membership share, what a rule scored out of sample reaches, with a lineage bootstrap; the design-corrected component ratio of the same collection, with an interval exact under the Gaussian one-way model by inversion of a noncentral F; and the superpopulation share for the species, with a chi-square layer on the number of lineages. Each is scored against its own truth on 135 simulated cells from five lineages to a thousand, and each sits behind a gate that refuses where the collection cannot identify the quantity or the residuals contradict the law the interval assumes, the coverage of each having been measured. A binary share is restated on the latent scale of the threshold model beside the observed scale. The lineage label may be a sequence type, a core-genome or SNP cluster, or a serovar, so the same estimate can be read at two typing resolutions. For a difference in non-wild-type prevalence between two collections it applies the Kitagawa decomposition to split the difference into a lineage-composition component and a within-lineage rate component, with a shared-support gate calibrated against measured interval coverage, a test for lineage labels that are differentially and informatively missing, and Benjamini-Yekutieli control within each component family of the antimicrobial panel, valid whatever the dependence between agents. Ships a Streptococcus suis case study (677 isolates, 650 porcine and 27 human, with full data provenance) read at population-cluster and at sequence-type resolution, together with a 720,000-decomposition calibration study and a head-to-head comparison against lineage-adjusted logistic regression. The package reads two tables and never a genome. A susceptibility panel is read at its recorded resolution: a dichotomised call and a recorded dilution are both intervals on the log2 concentration scale and enter one interval likelihood, so the input mode changes how much an observation carries rather than what is estimated. The interval is exact where every reading is a point and calibrated by simulation where a reading is an interval, and the tested wells are taken from the recorded values unless the panel is supplied. Each share carries an e-value; a run that declares the intake each isolate arrived in also carries the running product over intakes, a test supermartingale that may be read after any intake, with the panel decision taken on the log scale so that evidence too strong for a float is still evidence. False-discovery control across the panel holds under arbitrary dependence. The attribution is exercised outside the shipped cohorts on fifty organisms of one NCBI Pathogen Detection release, each taken at the release accession the retrieval recorded: every agent of every cohort that reaches the estimator leaves one record, estimated or refused with the condition that failed, 192 cells are estimated in twelve species and 44 admitted by the support gate in six, and every cell carries a permuted-label control. The Streptococcus suis cohort is read at three definitions of a lineage, population cluster, serotype and sequence type, with the reference label rerun on each other label's own isolates so that the label is separated from the collection. A veterinary arm cuts the same source by host species and by sampling matrix and runs every cell at two definitions of a lineage, the Pathogen Detection SNP cluster and the serovar, with the permuted-label control at both. items.title: amr-clonalshare: measuring how much of antimicrobial resistance travels with the clone

items.summary: Probabilistic seismic hazard and risk analyses are backbone to building codes, insurance pricing, and disaster management. Yet their open-engine pipelines remain accessible primarily to experts. We present the first agentic interface to the end-to-end probabilistic seismic hazard and risk chain via an open-source server, addressable through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). MCP wraps the OpenQuake engine and the 2020 European Seismic Hazard and Risk Models using twenty-four typed endpoints. Here, an agent is defined as a large language model (LLM) with tools. LLM is confined to the role of an orchestrator so it plans, translates, and explains, while the OpenQuake engine and custom codes compute hazard values, damage probability, and loss. Each response carries source-model, ground-motion model (GMM), and certified data provenance for transparency. Results are benchmarked against ESHM20 at seventy-three cities, the replicated 475-year spectral accelerations match official values within a median of 5 %, and a full hazard-to-loss estimate runs in minutes. The interface additionally accepts a user-supplied empirical or machine-learning GMM on any tectonic region type of the published tree, and adds additional features that existing web services omit: conditional spectra, deterministic scenarios, surface hazard, per-building loss, retrofit comparison, and record selection with waveform retrieval. The proposed design layers transfer to other regional models, and to other hazards.
items.title: An Agentic Interface for End-to-End Probabilistic Seismic Hazard and Risk Analysis

items.summary: This dataset accompanies “Population-scale burden analysis of rare damaging coding variants identifies novel risk genes for Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias and Parkinson’s disease and related disorders” by Le Guen, Peña-Tauber and colleagues. The release contains 16 gzip-compressed, tab-delimited gene-based burden summary-statistic files covering Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias (ADRD), Parkinson’s disease (PD), and Parkinson’s disease and related disorders (PDRD); combined-proxy and direct-diagnosis ascertainment; and all-ancestry (ALL) and European-ancestry (EUR) analyses. The files share 61 columns and contain 1,000,189 retained gene/mask analysis rows in total, including nonsignificant results. The four nested masks comprise high-confidence loss-of-function variants alone or together with qualifying missense variants at REVEL thresholds of 0.75, 0.50 or 0.25. The associated manuscript specifies GRCh38 coordinates. The primary discovery analyses are AD combined-proxy ALL and PD combined-proxy ALL. EUR analyses are secondary ancestry analyses; AD-direct and PD-direct are secondary, nested phenotype-sensitivity analyses. All ADRD/PDRD analyses are diagnostic-sensitivity comparisons. Combined-proxy includes direct cases and family-history-only proxy cases, not proxy cases alone. Phenotype definitions and ancestry strata overlap and are not independent replication datasets. The release explicitly separates effect estimation from association evidence. REGENIE-only effect estimates combine compatible binary-outcome burden models from UK Biobank, All of Us and ADSP for AD/ADRD, or UK Biobank, All of Us and AMP-PD for PD/PDRD. Combined-proxy cohort effects use the revised exact common-control mixture-model inversion under kappa=0.5. ADES stage-1 estimates from Holstege et al. (2022) are reported separately because their ordinal summed-dosage model differs from the REGENIE binary-outcome maximum-allele burden model. Eligible ADES and REGENIE results are integrated through effective-sample-size-weighted signed-Z evidence; no ADES-inclusive pooled odds ratio is calculated. Use P_OVERALL or LOG10P_OVERALL for final association evidence, and the BETA_REGENIE, SE_REGENIE and REGENIE odds-ratio/confidence-interval columns for the pooled REGENIE effect estimate. AD/ADRD overall evidence falls back to REGENIE when eligible ADES evidence is unavailable. ADES does not contribute to PD/PDRD. The same ADES source is reused across AD-family comparisons and ancestry strata. The README and column dictionary define all fields, missing-value conventions, numerical precision and interpretation. A public manifest and checksums document all 16 files. The dataset contains aggregate gene-level results, not individual-level genotypes or single-variant summary statistics. Dataset DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22702628. License selected for this record: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).
items.title: Population-scale burden analysis of rare damaging coding variants identifies novel risk genes for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias and Parkinson's disease and related disorders

items.summary: Training-data poisoning attacks can induce targeted, undetectable failure in deep neural networks by corrupting a vanishingly small fraction of training labels. We demonstrate this on acoustic vehicle classification using the MELAUDIS urban intersection dataset (approx. 9,600 audio clips, 6 classes): a compact 2-D convolutional neural network (CNN) trained on log-mel spectrograms achieves 95.7% Attack Success Rate (ASR) -- the fraction of target-class test samples misclassified under the attack -- on a Truck-to-Car label-flipping attack at just p=0.5% corruption (48 records), with zero detectable change in aggregate accuracy (87.6% baseline; 95% CI: 88-100%, n=3 seeds). We prove this stealth is structural: the maximum accuracy drop from a complete targeted attack is bounded above by the minority class fraction (beta). For real-world class imbalances (Truck approx. 3%), this bound falls below training-run noise, making aggregate accuracy monitoring provably insufficient regardless of architecture or attack method. A companion backdoor trigger attack reveals a novel trigger-dominance collapse: when the target class is a dataset minority, the spectrogram patch trigger becomes functionally redundant--clean ASR equals triggered ASR, and the attack degenerates to pure label flipping. We formalize the ML training pipeline as an attack surface and propose a trust-minimized defense combining content-addressed artifact hashing, Merkle-tree dataset commitment, and post-quantum digital signatures (ML-DSA-65/CRYSTALS-Dilithium3, NIST FIPS 204) for cryptographically verifiable data provenance.
items.title: Poisoned Acoustics

items.summary: Parametric models of the human head are essential tools traditionally used in computer vision and graphics for animation, rendering, and reconstruction. More recently, they serve as crucial conditioning signals within generative large vision models, allowing for tight spatial control of generated imagery. However, existing publicly available models are typically limited in anatomical scope, modeling only outer geometry while ignoring intra-oral and ocular structures, and frequently suffer from reduced geometric quality stemming from low-fidelity input datasets. In this report we introduce a new parametric model dubbed Generative aNthropometric Model (GNM), named as a homophone of the human genome. GNM encompasses the head, face, neck, eyeballs, teeth, and tongue, and it is built on an extensive database of high-resolution 3D scans combined with high-quality anatomy specific artist-made samples. This report details the data provenance, the model architecture including the specialized sub-models for the ocular and intra-oral structures, and shows its SotA performance on fitting target 3D face scans. To foster community innovation, the complete GNM framework is made publicly available.
items.title: GNM Head: A Generative aNthropometric Model of the human head

items.summary: Cloud Continuum applications require experimental environments capable of combining heterogeneous Edge, Fog, Cloud, and high-performance computing resources while preserving reproducibility, observability, and control over distributed deployments. This paper presents a two-level reference architecture for Cloud Continuum experimentation built on top of the SLICES Cloud Continuum Blueprint. The proposed approach separates the research-infrastructure layer, which exposes and manages distributed resources, from the application layer, where Cyber-Physical workflows are organized according to an Edge-Fog-Cloud pattern in which placement, timing, and data provenance are treated as first-class experimental concerns. The architecture is designed to support multiple continuum applications rather than a single domain-specific prototype. At the Edge, applications interact with physical devices and perform low-latency sensing or safety actions; at the Fog, they execute near-source coordination, mediation, and stream-processing logic; at the Cloud, they consolidate global knowledge through analytics, optimization, and visualization. This partitioning enables researchers to deploy, customize, and compare alternative control and monitoring strategies over the same programmable infrastructure substrate. The approach is validated through two representative use cases: Renewable Energy Community management, where distributed Digital Twin coordination and time-window-based energy control are requested, and AirWatch, a monitoring pipeline focused on anomaly detection, low-latency alerting, and cloud-side aggregation. Both workloads are evaluated through a systematic campaign of 40 runs comparing virtualized and physical edge deployments over a geographically distributed infrastructure.
items.title: A Cloud Continuum Research Infrastructure for Distributed CPS Experimentation

items.summary: Deterministic evidence archive accompanying the scworkbench preprint. It contains protocols, prompts and task cards, amendments, transfer and isolation records, inventories, provenance exports, validation reports, reproduction plans, scripts, receipts, equivalence results, resource records, operation-pack evidence, and five final or reproduced recipient bundles from the Honeybee, scPerturb and Xenopus-tail continuity experiments. The ten data shards and three control files were independently audited for deterministic construction, extraction, complete membership, checksums, privacy and path safety. Historical RC33, RC37 and RC38 runtime SIF binaries, the separately curated current publication SIF, and the original external WesselsSatija2023 H5AD are not included. Runtime identities and experiment assignments remain recorded. Read-only audit and later controller-executed reproduction remain distinct events. Rights apply per file and source. The scPerturb retained bundles include CC-BY-4.0 source attribution, operation-pack sources retain their MIT notices, and the deposit-level Other (Open) designation does not replace file-level notices. Archive integrity and terminal-policy acceptance do not establish biological validity, branch superiority, authenticated operator identity, source-byte verification at recipient boundaries, or universal reproducibility.
items.title: scworkbench cross-operator continuity experiments: evidence archive

items.summary: Modern large language model research agents, commonly marketed under the label deep research, are highly capable at locating sources, verifying claims, and synthesizing existing literature into structured reports. This capability has not translated into a comparable capacity for scientific discovery. We argue that this gap has a specific, testable cause, which we call literature attracti on: the more strongly a generation process is grounded in retrieved literature, the more its outputs converge toward concepts already dominant in that literature, at the expense of novelty. We separate four quantities that are routinely conflated in evaluations of AI research systems: research depth, research novelty, research validity, and research value. We review the current frontier of deep research systems and automated science pipelines, describe the attention-level mechanisms that plausibly cause literature attraction in retrieval-augmented generation, and propose a controlled experimental protocol to measure the novelty-grounding tradeoff dir ectly, using embedding-based and graph-based novelty metrics, a temporal hold-out benchmark, and human expert validation. We then outline an architectural response: a two-stage exploit-then-explore pipeline in which a quality-diversity search process is used to deliberately push hypothesis generation into regions of the concept space that are underrepresented in the retrieved literature, while an adversarial falsification agent constrains the resulting hypotheses to remain scientificall y testable. We close with a proposed output format, the research novelty report, that reports where a generated hypothesis sits relative to existing knowledge rather than asserting that it is novel. This paper is a research proposal and experimental design; it does not claim to have already demonstrated the phenomenon it sets out to measure.
items.title: Escaping the Literature: Exploring New Scientific Ideas with Large Language Models

items.summary: Abstract Background  Thyroid dysfunction is one of the most common endocrine disorders affecting metabolic activity, psychological well-being, and gastrointestinal function.(1,2) Patients frequently experience elevated thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) levels, stress, bloating, impaired digestion, reduced metabolic efficiency, and decreased quality of life. Although conventional treatment effectively restores thyroid hormone balance in many patients, complementary therapeutic interventions are increasingly being explored to improve overall clinical outcomes and patient-reported health status.  Aim  To evaluate the effect of a Teacurry Thyro Herb Tea for Thyroid on thyroid function, perceived stress, gastrointestinal symptoms, and participant-reported global improvement among adults with thyroid dysfunction.  Materials and Methods:  A prospective, single-arm interventional clinical study was conducted involving  22 adult participants  diagnosed with thyroid dysfunction. Baseline demographic characteristics including age, body weight, height, and body mass index (BMI) were recorded. Clinical assessments included serum thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), perceived stress score (0–40 scale), gastrointestinal symptoms related to bloating, digestion, and metabolism, and Participant Global Impression of Change (PGIC). All parameters were assessed before and after the intervention. The composition of the study formulation will be described separately. Statistical analysis was performed using appropriate descriptive and inferential statistical methods, and statistical significance was considered at  p  < 0.05.  Results:  The intervention demonstrated an overall improvement in multiple clinical outcomes. Mean serum TSH decreased from  10.27 to 3.77 mIU/L , while mean perceived stress scores decreased from  20.45 to 13.18 . Improvement in gastrointestinal symptoms and PGIC scores was observed in the majority of participants. Perceived stress scores decreased in a substantial proportion of participants, indicating improvement in psychological well-being. Gastrointestinal symptoms such as bloating and impaired digestion improved from mild or moderate severity to normal or minimal symptoms in the majority of cases. Participant-reported outcomes also demonstrated favorable changes, with PGIC scores increasing in most participants, suggesting meaningful overall clinical improvement. The intervention was generally well tolerated, and no serious adverse events were documented during the study period.  Conclusion:  The findings of this prospective clinical study suggest that the investigated Teacurry Thyro Herb Tea for Thyroid may contribute to improved thyroid function, reduction in perceived stress, better gastrointestinal health, and enhanced patient-reported quality of life in adults with thyroid dysfunction. These preliminary findings support the potential role of the formulation as a complementary therapeutic option. Larger randomized controlled clinical trials with extended follow-up are warranted to confirm these observations and establish long-term efficacy and safety.   Keywords: Thyroid Dysfunction; Thyroid Stimulating Hormone; TSH; Teacurry Thyro Herb Tea for Thyroid; Teacurry Thyroid Tea; Teacurry; Thyroid Tea; Herbal Tea for Thyroid; Complementary ##plugin
items.title: Effect of a Plant-Based Herbal Tea Formulation "Teacurry Thyro Herb Tea for Thyroid" on Thyroid Function, TSH Levels, Gastrointestinal Symptoms and Participant-Reported Global Improvement in Adults with Thyroid Dysfunction: Real-World Evidence Clinical Study

items.summary: Electric vehicles (EVs) experience significant  driving  range degradation in low ambient temperature conditions, primarily due to the elevated energy demand of heating system.  T his paper proposes  an optimal  control strategy for a  positive temperature coefficient ( PTC )  heater-based electric minibus  heating system ,  which is  aimed to  exploit actuators’ redundancy for  energy consumption  minimization  and driving range extension . The strategy  optimally  allocates  control inputs  of multiple actuators  to  provide  heating power demand ed  by a superimposed proportional-integral (PI)  feedback  controller of the  passenger  cabin air temperatur e .  The  optimal  allocation maps prescri be  coolant pump flow, blower air   flow, and inlet air temperature references , and they  are obtained by comprehensive simulations of a high-fidelity multi-physics heating system model over a wide range of quasi-stationary operating conditions .   A low-level PI controller is further designed for the full ,  allocation-related range of operating points to track the  allocated  inlet air temperature reference, while commanding the PTC heater power.   The overall control strategy is validated through co-simulation with a high-fidelity vehicle model  in comparison with an industry baseline strategy , demonstrating a considerable energy consumption reduction in both quasi-stationary and transient (heat up) conditions, as well as improved control performance in terms of shorter heat up intervals.
items.title: Optimal Control Allocation Strategy for an Energy-efficient PTC Heater-based Electric Vehicle Passenger Cabin Heating System

items.summary: Background: Surface roughness is an important characteristic of resin composite restorations and may be influenced by material composition and finishing and polishing procedures. Objective: To evaluate changes in surface roughness (Ra) of nanofilled, nanohybrid, and microhybrid resin composites after sequential finishing and polishing and to compare their final surface roughness. Materials and Methods: S ixty disc-shaped specimens (8 mm × 2 mm; shade A2) were fabricated using Filtek Z350 XT, IPS Empress Direct, and Filtek Z250 (n = 20 per material). Fifteen specimens per material underwent a standardized finishing and polishing protocol using fine- and extra-fine-grit diamond burs followed by sequential Sof-Lex discs, while five specimens per material remained untreated as controls. Surface roughness was measured using a Mitutoyo SJ-210 contact profilometer at baseline   and after the intervention. Because specimen-level identification was not preserved between measurement sessions, baseline and final measurements were analyzed as independent observations using independent-samples t-tests, with Welch’s correction when required. Final Ra values among materials were compared using one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey HSD tests (α = 0.05). Results: All three experimental composites showed statistically significant increases in Ra after finishing and polishing (all p < 0.001), whereas no statistically significant changes were observed in the untreated controls (all p > 0.05). Mean Ra increased from 0.085 to 0.181 μm for IPS Empress Direct, from 0.111 to 0.186 μm for Filtek Z350 XT, and from 0.122 to 0.195 μm for Filtek Z250. Final Ra values did not differ significantly among the three materials (F(2,42) = 0.559, p = 0.576). Conclusions: Sequential finishing and polishing significantly increased surface roughness relative to the strip-polymerized baseline surfaces of all three resin composites, without statistically significant differences in final Ra among the materials. The final mean Ra values remained below the predefined 0.2 μm surface-roughness threshold. Under the experimental conditions evaluated, post-polishing surface roughness could not be predicted solely on the basis of nanofilled, nanohybrid, or microhybrid filler classification.
items.title: Surface Roughness of Nanofilled, Nanohybrid, and Microhy-brid Resin Composites After Sequential Finishing and Polish-ing: An In Vitro Comparative Study

items.summary: Reliability Beyond Accuracy in Crop Classification Benchmarks (Supplementary Materials) Introduction: Near-perfect crop-label accuracy can conceal uncertainty, perturbation sensitivity, and weak explanations. This study evaluates these reliability dimensions without treating benchmark classification as agronomic recommendation. Materials and Methods: Ten classifiers were evaluated using five matched stratified fitting, validation, and test partitions on a 2,200-record crop-label benchmark and an independent 3,810-record rice-grain benchmark. A Calibrated Selective Forest combined Random Forest, validation-fitted temperature scaling, and confidence-based abstention. Analyses included feature and component ablations, probability calibration, Gaussian input perturbations, computational cost, and explanation fidelity. Results: Mean crop-label accuracy was 99.59% for Random Forest, 99.23% for XGBoost, and 98.32% for FT-Transformer. Random Forest calibration reduced mean expected calibration error from 0.0449 to 0.0038. At a 0.95 threshold, calibrated selection retained 98.59% of predictions with 0.091% mean selective error. Under perturbations of 0.20 training standard deviations, its accuracy fell to 86.96% and selective error rose to 4.29%. On rice grains, Random Forest accuracy was 91.71%, and calibration did not improve every probability metric. Local explanation rankings were often stable despite a median neighborhood weighted R² of 0.293 under the specified local interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LIME) configuration. Conclusions: Accuracy, calibration, selective reliability, and explanation fidelity are distinct properties. The composite pipeline provides an auditable benchmark procedure, not a new learning algorithm or a validated farm recommendation system. Geographic and temporal agronomic validation remain necessary.
items.title: Reliability Beyond Accuracy in Crop Classification Benchmarks (Supplementary Materials)

items.summary: PIHR-RH-XXVII reduced the arithmetic obstruction in the Prime Integrator-Holonomy-Recursion (PIHR) programme to a sharply localized centered endpoint-plus-tail functional after exact removal of the divergent harmonic prime spine. The present paper develops the subsequent analysis and records several new exact identities, structural no-go results, and a substantially weaker sufficient arithmetic target. First, a new nonlinear crossing storage is introduced. It is constant between prime-power impulses and telescopes exactly to an exponential expression involving the reciprocal von Mangoldt sum and the critical square-root-weighted von Mangoldt sum. At an interpolated Euler-constant downcrossing the nonlinear storage coincides with the critical tangent. This gives a compact exponential Euler formulation of the crossing problem. Second, a first-contact analysis of the Jordan-Riesz deformation shows that the Laplace moment route does not by itself bypass the critical sign problem: complete monotonicity of the limiting moment function would essentially re-encode positivity of the underlying tangent. An interval version of the Jordan deformation nevertheless removes a different obstruction, namely numerator cancellation at hypothetical off-critical zeta zeros. The subsequent fixed-parameter transfer audit shows why asymptotic Selberg production dominance does not automatically imply positivity of the centered Jordan-Riesz state: after complete subtraction of the elementary finite-Euler modes, the same harmonic 1/p   prime-spine operator reappears independently of the deformation parameter. Third, a direct energy calculation at an exact Euler-constant crossing yields a new identity for the tangent J(T) . The identity separates a positive quadratic history, a positive diagonal contribution, and a single ordered impulse-history correlation. Polarization of that correlation produces an exact nonnegative pair-dispersion energy. Splitting the pair interaction at the multiplicative hyperbola  mn = x   then separates a causal Selberg pair sector from an overdiagonal sector. The causal sector is controlled by genuine positive multiplicative pair production, while the overdiagonal sector becomes an exact complementary-scale deficit difference D(T-t)-D(t) , exhibiting a largest-prime/least-prime duality consistent with the finite-Euler analysis of PIHR-RH-XXVI. Finally, the Landau endpoint is weakened. Exact eventual positivity of J   is stronger than necessary: under the stated transform-continuation hypotheses, a lower bound J(T)>-e o(T)    already excludes every hypothetical zeta zero with real part greater than 1/2. Consequently the remaining arithmetic problem need not orient the centered pair-transport remainder pointwise; it is sufficient to bound its negative part subexponentially. This is a materially weaker target than the crossing inequality itself. The principal remaining problem is an unconditional subexponential one-sided estimate for the centered overdiagonal Selberg pair transport, preserving its multiplicative orientation after the linear prime-spine telescope.
items.title: Crossing Energy, Ordered Selberg Pair Transport, and a Subexponential Landau Reduction of the Remaining Riemann-Hypothesis Obstruction

items.summary: This reproducibility package accompanies a measurement-science workflow for temporal light modulation (TLM) metric reproduction and computational sensitivity analysis. Five independent MK350S Premium optical waveform records form the bounded commercial demonstration. MetTLM W1–W20 public references support source-traceable PstLM/SVM calculation-pipeline reproduction and sampling-rate, duration and deterministic modelled-effect sensitivity analyses. Evidence identity is preserved so that public waveforms, resampled/windowed/perturbed rows and auxiliary electrical/photometric records are not treated as additional commercial observations. The package includes the five commercial raw waveform files, machine-readable commercial/context summaries, source code, public-reference provenance and checksums, frozen MetTLM reproduction outputs, sampling/duration/modelled-effect outputs, journal-neutral numerical and claim-boundary QC files and a journal-neutral manuscript snapshot. Raw third-party public-reference assets and manufacturer documents are intentionally not redistributed; original DOI/license/checksum provenance and reconstruction scripts are provided instead. The package supports calculation-pipeline reproduction and bounded commercial SVM-related screening. It does not constitute IEC certification, physical calibration, commercial-lamp PstLM, measurement uncertainty, commercial repeatability, PF–SVM causality or population-level generalization.
items.title: Reproducibility Package for Public-Reference Reproduction and Sensitivity Analysis of Temporal Light Modulation Metrics Using MetTLM

items.summary: Code, frozen configurations, leakage-aware split manifests, lightweight run records, statistical tables, figure source data, and checksums for a three-dataset open-set bearing-fault diagnosis benchmark. Third-party raw vibration data and trained model checkpoints are not redistributed.
items.title: Reproducibility package for Open-Set Bearing-Fault Diagnosis Rankings Across Datasets

items.summary: Processed data and analysis code supporting “Horizontal wind estimation from consumer-drone hover telemetry: comparing machine-learning and calibration approaches.” The dataset covers 50 DJI Air 3S hover sessions at two sites in Bremen, Germany, with reference wind measurements from a TriSonica Mini ultrasonic anemometer. The study compares Ridge regression with a tilt-based calibration baseline for estimating horizontal wind from drone telemetry. The archive includes aligned 10 Hz data, derived features, calibration measurements, fitted models, held-out predictions, validation metrics, and processing and plotting scripts. Raw flight and anemometer logs are not included but are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.
items.title: Wind estimation from DJI Air 3S hover telemetry: dataset and code

items.summary: European digital sovereignty and security increasingly depend on whether high-impact decisions can be grounded in location evidence that remains credible under adversarial pressure. This paper frames a cross-sector analysis as a location-data provenance problem: whether there is contestable evidence about where and when an asserted event occurred, who or what produced the assertion, what a device or service reported as location, and which audit and retention guarantees apply. Trust-erosion patterns are observable across democratic processes and the information environment, trade and origin-sensitive supply chains, finance and illicit shipping flows, critical infrastructure and mobility, and harms targeting individuals' private and social domains. In these patterns we see a recurring asymmetry in which locality, presence, routing, or jurisdiction can be asserted cheaply while institutions and affected parties face costly reconstruction when disputes arise. To make this challenge actionable, this paper introduces a compact risk taxonomy that decomposes provenance failures into integrity axes and recurring failure modes, and derives design expectations for next-generation digital trust infrastructure centered on contestability under dispute, while remaining privacy- and rights-compatible. It argues for treating location as a digital primitive that should be represented as evidence-bearing claims rather than self-asserted coordinates, and positions proof-of-location (PoL) mechanisms as a candidate capability layer for producing verifiable presence claims under explicit threat and privacy assumptions. The outcome is a sector-neutral foundation for future architectural work on a next-generation digital trust infrastructure for Europe.
items.title: Where Trust Fails: Mapping Location-Data Provenance Risks in Europe

items.summary: A provenance analysis for a query evaluation or a model checking computation extracts information on how its result depends on the atomic facts of the model or database. Traditional work on data provenance was, to a large extent, restricted to positive query languages or the negation-free fragment of first-order logic and showed how provenance abstractions can be usefully described as elements of commutative semirings -- most generally as multivariate polynomials with positive integer coefficients. We describe and evaluate here a provenance approach for dealing with negation, based on quotient semirings of polynomials with dual indeterminates. This not only provides a semiring provenance analysis for full first-order logic (and other logics and query languages with negation) but also permits a reverse provenance analysis, i.e., finding models that satisfy various properties under given provenance tracking assumptions. We describe the potential for applications to explaining missing query answers or failures of integrity constraints, and to using these explanations for computing repairs. This approach also is the basis of a systematic study of semiring semantics in a broad logical context.
items.title: Provenance Analysis and Semiring Semantics for First-Order Logic

items.summary: This repository provides the supplementary materials and reproducibility package for the manuscript “Spatial–Temporal Hedging in Cross-Border Logistics under Heterogeneous Evidence Quality: A Wasserstein DRO Approach.” The repository contains the computational inputs, scenario data, experimental results, source code, and supplementary numerical outputs used in the study. It includes materials for the baseline experiments, credibility and ambiguity-radius sensitivity analyses, out-of-sample evaluations, spatial–temporal hedging ablation experiments, rolling-information tests, and computational scalability analysis. The materials are provided to support transparency, verification, and reproducibility of the numerical experiments reported in the manuscript.
items.title: Data and Code for "Spatial–Temporal Hedging in Cross-Border Logistics under Heterogeneous Evidence Quality: A Wasserstein DRO Approach"

items.summary: Per-pixel  active-flame  image–mask chips from  Sentinel-2  covering  25 large California wildfires  (acquisitions spanning 2020–2026). The deposit contains  2,148  co-registered pairs of false-colour composites and segmentation masks. Each chip is  512 × 512 pixels at 20 m  (~10.24 km across), rendered as a fixed-stretch RGB composite ( R = B12 / SWIR2 ,  G = B11 / SWIR1 ,  B = B8A / NIR ) so flaming combustion is separable from cloud, smoke, fresh char, and bright reflective surfaces. Masks were generated automatically with a  modified HOTMAP SWIR hotspot rule  (confirmed flame where B12 and B12/B8A exceed conservative thresholds, plus a connected growth tier for cooler front margins). Pixel values are  0 = background ,  1 = active fire , and  255 = no-data  (outside the acquisition footprint). The corpus uses a  leak-free fire holdout : whole incidents are assigned to partitions ( 18 train / 3 validation / 4 test ), so evaluation measures transfer to unseen fires rather than random chips from the same landscape. This archive includes: images/  and  masks/  (2,148 PNG files each) summary.csv  (chip-level metadata) partitions.csv  (fire → split assignment) analyst_review/hand_masks/  ( 233  independently reviewed test chips;  54%  of the test split), for quantifying weak-label agreement at chip/cluster level Companion  code , labelling protocol, baseline training scripts, and manuscript figures are available at:   https://github.com/MohammadrezaNarimaniUCDavis/California_Sentinel2_Active_Fire_Dataset This dataset supports a data article prepared for submission to  Data in Brief (Elsevier).
items.title: California Sentinel-2 Active-Fire Segmentation Dataset

items.summary: The coordination of Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) in high-density industrial environments represents a critical challenge within Logistics 4.0, as traditional traffic management methods often lead to inefficiencies caused by negotiation-based priority assignment. To overcome the resulting limitations, this paper presents an innovative AGV traffic management system based on a Lifelong Multi-Agent Path Finding (L-MAPF) algorithm operating on roadmaps generated with Non-Uniform Rational B-Splines (NURBS) curves. The approach guarantees locally optimal coordination and ensures safe operation of large and heterogeneous AGVs. Building on this concept, the proposed framework integrates a modified version of the Bounded Horizon Conflict Based Search (CBS) technique within a Rolling Horizon Conflict Resolution strategy, utilizing an extended time horizon for each agent to enable effective conflict resolution in corridors identified by a topological map. In contrast to state-of-the-art methods for AGV fleet traffic management, the proposed solution is designed for real-world, non-standardized (i.e., non-grid-like) industrial settings characterized by narrow bidirectional corridors and high-traffic density, where AGVs of various sizes and capabilities operate simultaneously. Key contributions include an anytime conflict resolution strategy with adaptive time horizon regulation, an execution layer for safe and standard-compliant interaction with real AGVs, and an advanced mechanism for deadlock detection and resolution. Experimental results obtained in realistic industrial environments demonstrate higher throughput, with improvements of up to 11% over a conventional rule-based traffic management system, a state-of-the-art industrial method, and a priority-based L-MAPF variant, while maintaining continuous operation and improved efficiency.
items.title: A traffic management system for large and heterogeneous vehicles in narrow industrial environments

items.summary: This deposit contains the results replication package for the article “Governing the Eurasian Roundabout: Anti-Circumvention Governance and Post-Soviet Intermediaries after 2022.” It reconstructs the article’s quantitative trade evidence from archived Eurostat Easy Comext data and provides structured versions of all numbered tables and figures. The product-specific analysis covers monthly EU27 exports from January 2019 through December 2025 for the 50 six-digit Harmonized System codes in the February 2024 Common High Priority Items list and 13 destinations. The workflow constructs the balanced product–partner–month panel, aggregates partner–month exports, calculates raw and normalized summaries, compares product-specific growth with total-export growth, estimates descriptive partner- and month-fixed-effects paths, and reproduces the reported comparison windows and sensitivity checks. The reconstructed evidence shows a sharp contraction in mean monthly EU exports of Common High Priority Items to Russia, from EUR 295.7 million in 2021 to EUR 3.3 million in 2023–2025, alongside increases from EUR 13.934 million to EUR 30.835 million for Kazakhstan and from EUR 1.319 million to EUR 4.496 million for Armenia. Product-specific export growth exceeded total-export growth in both focal destinations, by 14.1 index points in Kazakhstan and 74.2 index points in Armenia. The package also reproduces the pre-event diagnostic, late-2021 contrast, alternative normalizations, product and comparison-set checks, alternative windows, destination distribution, and descriptive policy-milestone summaries. These results are descriptive and corroborative. They do not identify onward shipment, circumvention, ultimate buyers or end users, enforcement effectiveness, or causal policy effects. The archived product-specific and total-export series come from different Eurostat data vintages, and the broad comparison is interpreted accordingly. Run the complete analysis from the extracted package directory with one command: python3 reproduce.py This deposit is associated with the results package at https://zenodo.org/records/19206576 that supports former version of the article.
items.title: Governing the Eurasian Roundabout: Anti-Circumvention Governance and Post-Soviet Intermediaries after 2022. V2

items.summary: This repository contains supplementary documentation for a qualitative interview study examining how Bachelor of Software Engineering students understand and use generative AI in their studies. The study investigates: (1) the roles students assign to generative AI and how these roles are enacted; (2) how generative AI transforms learning and software-development tasks and how students legitimize its adoption; and (3) how students negotiate and exercise agency when working with generative AI. The package includes: the interview guide and replication material; First Cycle codebooks organized by research question; Second Cycle Pattern Codes and explanations of their analytical development; a code-saturation monitoring record tracing code emergence, elaboration, and confirmation across interviews; and supplementary evidence tables supporting the reported findings. The interviews were analyzed using the two-cycle coding approach described by Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña. First Cycle coding combined descriptive, process, and values-oriented codes. During Second Cycle analysis, conceptually related First Cycle codes were synthesized into broader Pattern Codes. Interview recordings and full transcripts are not publicly available because they contain potentially identifying contextual information and were collected under confidentiality commitments. The package therefore supports analytical transparency and methodological replication without releasing the underlying confidential data. The materials should be interpreted in relation to the educational and institutional context reported in the associated publication. The codebooks and Pattern Codes represent an inductively developed analytical framework rather than a universal taxonomy of student AI adoption.

items.summary: Replication data and code for an analysis of how allocation procedures shape which Italian municipalities obtain Recovery and Resilience Facility resources, and whether they convert them into completed works. The package covers 68,990 projects implemented by municipal governments across 36 plan measures, extracted from the OpenPNRR REST API at the ReGiS extraction date of 13 June 2026. Each project carries a coded allocation regime — open window, competitive, administrative assignment, or decentralised regional selection — reconstructed from the administrative activation procedure and, where that field is blank, from the founding decrees of the measures concerned. Contents: the analytical dataset (31 variables); a codebook; a procedure coding table with the normative source of every coding decision; a crosswalk matching 39 measures to the official monitoring of the statutory 40 per cent Southern allocation obligation; municipality-level residuals from the implementation models; global Moran's I under three alternative spatial weight matrices; local Moran statistics on the downstream residual; the reported model results; the extraction script; and a replication script that reproduces the dataset and every estimate from the raw inputs. WHY THIS PACKAGE IS NECESSARY. The primary source is neither versioned nor stable. While this dataset was being constructed, the same endpoint returned 280,767 records dated 26 February 2026 and, hours later, 291,387 records dated 13 June 2026, while the published CSV files carried 298,338 records; between those two responses the numeric identifiers of both projects and implementing organisations were reassigned. A replication attempt that re-downloaded from source would not reproduce these figures, and no version parameter is available to request a specific extraction. The archived snapshot in this package is the only reproducible reference. TWO TRAPS THAT FAIL SILENTLY. ISTAT codes and fiscal codes lose leading zeros if read as numeric, producing empty joins with no error; in the source organisation register, fiscal codes are stored inconsistently with and without leading zeros, and normalising to eleven digits reduces 13,126 records labelled as municipalities to 7,902 distinct entities. Numeric project identifiers are not stable join keys, coinciding across extractions in only 52.9 per cent of cases; the CUP is not unique. Use the local project code. SPATIAL ANALYSIS. Municipal geometries are the official Istat boundaries at 1 January 2021, joined on the six-digit code. The boundary file is not redistributed here and should be obtained from Istat. Three weight matrices are reported — queen contiguity, eight nearest neighbours and a fifty-kilometre distance band — because they are not interchangeable on subsamples: queen contiguity strands as isolates not only islands but mainland municipalities whose neighbours do not belong to the subsample, and those units are dropped silently from the statistic. Isolate counts are reported for every specification. The duration residual was the pre-specified primary diagnostic and the downstream residual was examined subsequently; both are reported in that order. The package contains no personal data: all implementing bodies are public administrations.
items.title: Allocation regimes and the territorial conversion of recovery funds: replication package for 71,548 municipal projects under Italy's National Recovery and Resilience Plan

items.summary: Provenance plays a crucial role in scientific workflow execution, for instance by providing data for failure analysis, real-time monitoring, or statistics on resource utilization for right-sizing allocations. The workflows themselves, however, become increasingly complex in terms of involved components. Furthermore, they are executed on distributed cluster infrastructures, which makes the real-time collection, integration, and analysis of provenance data challenging. Existing provenance systems struggle to balance scalability, real-time processing, online provenance analytics, and integration across different components and compute resources. Moreover, most provenance solutions are not workflow-aware; by focusing on arbitrary workloads, they miss opportunities for workflow systems where optimization and analysis can exploit the availability of a workflow specification that dictates, to some degree, task execution orders and provides abstractions for physical tasks at a logical level. In this paper, we present HyProv, a hybrid provenance management system that combines centralized and federated paradigms to offer scalable, online, and workflow-aware queries over workflow provenance traces. HyProv uses a centralized component for efficient management of the small and stable workflow-specification-specific provenance, and complements this with federated querying over different scalable monitoring and provenance databases for the large-scale execution logs. This enables low-latency access to current execution data. Furthermore, the design supports complex provenance queries, which we exemplify for the workflow system Airflow in combination with the resource manager Kubernetes. Our experiments indicate that HyProv scales to large workflows, answers provenance queries with sub-second latencies, and adds only modest CPU and memory overhead to the cluster.
items.title: HyProv: Hybrid Provenance Management for Scientific Workflows

items.summary: L'Ange des projections lumineuses was a monthly journal published for the Œuvre des projections catéchistiques of Champtercier (Basses-Alpes), printed at Lyon, and edited by the abbé Georges Aillaud. It ran from 15 October 1902 to 15 September 1903 as the organ of a subscription lending library that circulated magic-lantern slide sets to village clergy, together with the technical advice, lecture texts and equipment notices needed to use them. This deposit is a complete transcription of the ten issues held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France — 198 pages. Numbers 10 and 11, July and August 1903, are absent from the BnF holdings and no copies have been located elsewhere. The journal documents a working provincial distribution network at the moment cinema was arriving in rural France: it lists the slide sets in circulation and their prices, reports what was shown and where, argues over illuminants and apparatus, and by its final number is advertising a cinematograph alongside the lantern equipment. Its technical columns are a detailed record of alcohol, Auer and acetylene illumination in non-commercial exhibition. Method. The text was read from the BnF's page images by a vision language model working on overlapping half-page tiles, without optical character recognition, and then compared word by word by machine against the BnF's own OCR text layer wherever one exists. 1,864 disagreements were found across the 150 pages with a text layer, classified automatically, and checked selectively — not exhaustively — against the page images; eight readings were corrected as a result, and a separate audit for digital artefacts produced a further fifty. Every correction is logged with its evidence. This is machine transcription with editorial checking: it has not been proofread cover to cover against the original and should not be described as though it had. The February, March and April 1903 issues have no BnF text layer, rest on a single reading, and are identified as such. Spelling, accentuation, capitalisation and punctuation follow the page, including where the printing is inconsistent with itself. Contents of this deposit. The reading edition as PDF (119 pp.) and as plain UTF-8 text, both carrying the editorial note as front matter; the per-page source files, which preserve the printed line breaks and their end-of-line hyphens, with the flags raised on each page and a separate folder for the eighteen non-journal leaves; the editorial note; an apparatus of 137 unresolved or adjudicated readings; the full correction log; and the complete uncurated production log, labelled as provenance documentation rather than an apparatus. See README.md. Source. Bibliothèque nationale de France, shelfmark D-72088 (BIS); ISSN 2273-6220; BnF catalogue record cb326930724. Page images: Source gallica.bnf.fr / Bibliothèque nationale de France . Rights. The journal text is in the public domain. The editorial note, annotations, arrangement and other original editorial contributions are licensed under CC BY 4.0 . No copyright is asserted over the underlying public-domain text. Related. A prose introduction to the journal — its publisher, the slide network it served, and its bearing on the arrival of cinema in provincial France — was published at the time of this deposit at billlefurgy.com/ange-des-projections-lumineuses . It is not part of this deposit and is not covered by the method statement above.
items.title: L'Ange des projections lumineuses: Transcription of the Ten Issues Held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France, 1902–1903

items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are trained through multi-stage pipelines over heterogeneous data sources, yet developers lack a principled way to pinpoint the specific data responsible for an observed behavior. This lack of observability reduces debugging to reactive patching and makes failures prone to recur under distribution shift or subsequent model updates. To address this limitation, we propose DebugLM, a framework that equips LLMs with built-in data provenance, enabling them to explicitly trace the origins of their behaviors to specific training data sources. Specifically, the model learns to associate its responses with unique provenance tags that indicate the responsible dataset, empowering developers to precisely identify where undesirable behaviors are learned. Building on this capability, DebugLM further supports targeted test-time remediation, enabling developers to selectively trigger targeted refusal for specified data sources without retraining or modifying model parameters. Experiments demonstrate that DebugLM provides accurate behavior tracing in multi-stage training pipelines and effective test-time remediation while preserving the general utility of the model.
items.title: DebugLM: Learning Traceable Training Data Provenance for LLMs

items.summary: Welcome to WARP WARP (WDL Analysis Research Pipelines) repository is a collection of cloud-optimized pipelines for processing biological data from the Broad Institute Data Sciences Platform and collaborators. The contents of this repository are open source and released under the BSD 3-Clause license . Table of Contents WARP Overview Navigating WARP Using WARP WARP Versioning and Releasing Testing in WARP Feedback Acknowledgements WARP Overview WARP pipelines provide robust, standardized data analysis for the Broad Institute Genomics Platform and large consortia like the Human Cell Atlas and the BRAIN Initiative. You can count on WARP for rigorously scientifically validated, high scale, reproducible and open source pipelines. Our pipelines are written as "workflows" using the Workflow Description Language (WDL) and they process a broad spectrum of "omic" and array-related datasets (see the overview table below). | Pipeline Category | Data Types | | --- | --- | | Germline Variant Discovery | Genomes, Exomes | | Genotyping Arrays | Variant discovery, Chip validation, Joint array analysis | | Single-cell/nuclei Transcriptomics | Droplet based (10x Genomics), Smartseq2 | | Single-cell Epigenomics | Single nuclei ATAC-seq, Single nuclei MethylC-seq | | Joint Genotyping | Genomes, Exomes | | Somatic Alignment (beta) | Exomes | Try our pipelines in Terra , a platform for collaborative cloud analysis! Learn how in the Using WARP section. Navigating WARP All versioned and released pipelines are in one of the three pipelines subdirectories: broad (pipelines for the Broad Institute's Genomics Platform), cemba (pipelines for the BRAIN Initiative) or skylab (pipelines for the Human Cell Atlas Project). Each pipeline directory hosts a main workflow WDL that includes a pipeline version number and a corresponding changelog file. Workflows may call additional WDLs, referred to as tasks, that are located in the tasks directory. Pipelines that are in progress or have not yet been validated are in the beta-pipelines folder. Using WARP There are three ways to use WARP pipelines: 1. Download the workflow and run on a WDL-compatible execution engine WDL workflows run on multiple systems, including Cromwell , miniWDL , and dxWDL (see the openwdl documentation ). To run a pipeline's latest release, first navigate to WARP Releases , search for your pipeline's tag, and download the pipeline's assets (the WDL workflow, the JSON, and the ZIP with accompanying dependencies; see Optimus example below). You can also access a pipeline's release page by selecting the pipeline version number at the top of the pipeline's README. After downloading the pipeline's assets, launch the workflow following your execution engine's instructions. 2. Run the pipeline in Terra Several WARP pipelines are available in public workspaces on the Terra cloud platform. These workspaces include both the WDL workflow and downsampled data so that you can test the pipeline at low-cost. If you are new to Terra, you can get started by registering with your Google account and visiting Terra Support . After registration, search for WARP-related workspaces with the "warp-pipelines" tag. To test the pipeline, clone (make a copy of) the workspace following the instructions in this Terra Support guide . 3. Run or export the pipeline from Dockstore Dockstore is a GA4GH compliant open platform for sharing Docker-based tools like WDL workflows. You can find WARP pipelines in Dockstore and run them on the Dockstore platform or export them to other platforms (including Terra). To view all available pipelines, just search "warp" in the Dockstore search and browse the workflow list. See Dockstore documentation for details on launching the workflow. items.summary: SlideRule is an open source server-side framework for on-demand processing of science data in the cloud. The SlideRule project offers a new paradigm for NASA archival data management – rapid delivery of customizable on-demand data products, rather than hosting large volumes of standard derivative products, which will inevitably be insufficient for some science applications. The scalable server-side components of SlideRule run in the AWS cloud with optimized functions to read HDF5 data hosted by NASA in S3 cloud object storage. While SlideRule can be accessed by any HTTP client (e.g., curl) through GET and POST requests, the sliderule-python client provides a user-friendly API for synchronous interaction with the SlideRule service. The client library returns standard Python data containers (i.e., Pandas DataFrame) and facilitates serialization with provenance metadata for reproducible science. SlideRule uses a plugin framework to support different NASA missions and data products. The ICESat-2 SlideRule plugin offers customizable algorithms to process the archive of low-level data products from the NASA Ice Cloud and land Elevation Satellite-2 (ICESat-2) laser altimetry mission. The user defines a geographic area of interest and key processing parameters via an interactive web interface or the API, and SlideRule returns high-level surface elevation point cloud products in seconds to minutes, enabling rapid algorithm development, visualization and scientific interpretation.
